title: Finite normalization limit of a good bounded formal prime family
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian Nagata integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], and let $x\in A$ be nonzero and not a unit. Assume $A$ is $(x)$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix a nonempty finite subset $\gamma_0\subset\operatorname{Max}A$, and let $\Gamma_0$ be all finite subsets $\gamma\subset\operatorname{Max}A$ containing $\gamma_0$. Put $A_\gamma=(A\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak m\in\gamma}\mathfrak m)^{-1}A$, the ring of fractions with denominators outside those maximal ideals, and $D_\gamma=\varprojlim_{j\ge1}A_\gamma/x^jA_\gamma$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose primes $p_\gamma\subset D_\gamma$ satisfy $p_\gamma\cap A=(0)$ and the following compatibility: for $\gamma\subseteq\delta$, the inverse image of $p_\gamma$ under $D_\delta\to D_\gamma$ is $p_\delta$. Assume also $p_\gamma=p_\delta D_\gamma$ for every $\gamma\subseteq\delta$. Let $E_\gamma$ be the integral closure of $D_\gamma/p_\gamma$ in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The injective quotient maps $D_\delta/p_\delta\to D_\gamma/p_\gamma$ extend to fraction fields and induce maps $E_\delta\to E_\gamma$. Define $T=\varprojlim_{\gamma\in\Gamma_0}E_\gamma$, explicitly the ring of tuples $(e_\gamma)_\gamma$ compatible with these maps. Suppose $\Delta=\bigcup_{\gamma\in\Gamma_0}\{Q\cap A:Q\text{ is prime minimal over }xE_\gamma\}$ is finite. Then the canonical map $A\to T$ is injective, $T$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, and every prime $q$ minimal over $xT$ satisfies $q\cap A\in\Delta$.

source.place: J. Nishimura and T. Nishimura, Ideal-adic Completion of Noetherian Rings II, Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra II (1988), pp.453–467. Definitions 1.1–1.6 and Lemmas 1.10–1.17, pp.456–460, the normalization-limit construction in the proof of Theorem 1.9; in particular Lemma 1.11(1.11.1) and Lemmas 1.15 and 1.17.

proof.text: For each $P\in\Delta$ choose a maximal ideal containing $P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Adjoin these finitely many maximal ideals to $\gamma_0$, obtaining $\eta$. Every coordinate $A\to D_\gamma/p_\gamma\hookrightarrow E_\gamma$ is injective because $p_\gamma\cap A=0$. These maps are compatible, so their tuple map $A\to T$ is injective. Each $E_\gamma$ is a domain, and the image of $x$ is nonzero; multiplication by $x$ is therefore injective on $T$ as well.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology; coordinate argument written explicitly.

proof.text: Each $A_\gamma$ is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization], hence Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], $D_\gamma$ is complete and Noetherian. The quotient $A_\gamma/xA_\gamma$ is Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata]. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] it is $D_\gamma/xD_\gamma$. Apply [lem-per-adic-nagata-lifting] to see that $D_\gamma$ is Nagata. Its prime quotient $C_\gamma=D_\gamma/p_\gamma$ is N-2 by [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring]; [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] with the degree-one fraction-field extension makes $E_\gamma$ finite over $C_\gamma$, and hence finite over $D_\gamma$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-complete-over-complete-noetherian] makes every $E_\gamma$ complete and separated for powers of $x$.

source.place: Tags 032U, 05GG, 0316, 032T, 032R and 032F; Marot lifting as cited in lem-per-adic-nagata-lifting.

proof.text: The ring $T$ is $x$-adically separated: if $t\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}x^nT$, then $\pi_\gamma(t)\in\bigcap_nx^nE_\gamma=0$ by Step 2 for every $\gamma$. Thus all coordinates of $t$ vanish, so $t=0$.

source.place: Agent coordinate argument using the separatedness established in Step 2.

proof.text: Put $E=E_\eta$. It is Noetherian: any ideal is a $D_\eta$-submodule of the finite module $E$, so has finitely many $D_\eta$-generators by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]; the same elements generate it as an $E$-ideal. It is a normal domain by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], applied to $C_\eta=D_\eta/p_\eta$ and its own fraction field. By [lem-trf-normalization-integral-closure-krull] it is Krull, and [lem-trf-krull-principal-primary-decomposition] gives finitely many height-one primes $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$ over $x$, with $xE=\bigcap_i(E\cap xE_{Q_i})$. These are exactly the primes minimal over $xE$: the radicals of the primary components are the $Q_i$, which are incomparable height-one primes. If $s=0$, then $xE=E$; [lem-per-formal-boundary-power-detection] at $n=1$ gives $T=xT$, contradicting Steps 1 and 3. Thus $s>0$. Write $P_i=Q_i\cap A\in\Delta$.

source.place: Agent setup using Theorem 4.10.5 and Proposition 4.10.3, printed pp.89–91; normality is Stacks Tag 034L; module subobjects are Tag 00IK.

proof.text: For each $i$, put $R_i=A/P_i$, $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(R_i)$ and $L_i=\operatorname{Frac}(E/Q_i)$. Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] give a finite injective ring map $(R_i)_\eta\to E/Q_i$, where $(R_i)_\eta$ denotes localization at the image of $A\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak m\in\eta}\mathfrak m$. Injectivity is the definition of $P_i$; finiteness follows by quotienting the finite $D_\eta$-module $E$, using $x\in Q_i$ and $D_\eta/xD_\eta=A_\eta/xA_\eta$. Localizing at all nonzero elements of $R_i$ gives a finite-dimensional domain over $K_i$, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]; it contains $E/Q_i$ and is inside its fraction field, so equals $L_i$. Therefore $L_i/K_i$ is finite. By [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] the domain $R_i$ is N-2; [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] gives a finite $R_i$-module $N_i$, its integral closure in $L_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $N_i$ is integrally closed in $L_i$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(N_i)=L_i$.

source.place: Agent residue-field bound from Tags 05GG, 032R, 032F and 034L; finite-dimensional-domain field criterion is rank–nullity.

proof.text: Every $t\in T$ has residue $\overline{t_\eta}\in N_i\subset L_i$. To prove this, fix any prime $\mathfrak r$ of $R_i$, let $\mathfrak p$ be its inverse image in $A$, and choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Set $\delta=\eta\cup\{\mathfrak m\}$. The composite $E_\delta\to E_\eta\to L_i$ sends $t_\delta$ to $\overline{t_\eta}$. Since $E_\delta$ is finite over $D_\delta$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] supplies a monic relation for $t_\delta$ over $D_\delta$. In $L_i$ this relation factors through $D_\delta/xD_\delta=A_\delta/xA_\delta$ by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. Its coefficients therefore lie in $(R_i)_\mathfrak r$: every allowed denominator avoids $\mathfrak m$, hence avoids $\mathfrak p$. Thus $\overline{t_\eta}$ is integral over every $(R_i)_\mathfrak r$, and [lem-sfb-integral-element-prime-local-criterion], with ambient algebra $L_i$, makes it integral over $R_i$. It belongs to $N_i$ by definition. This compares residues using every enlarged coordinate, not only $\eta$.

source.place: Agent comparison of coordinate residues, using Tags 00E0, 00GK, 05GG and 034K (lemma-integral-closure-stalks).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel], each $E_{Q_i}$ is a discrete valuation ring with normalized valuation $v_i$; choose a uniformizer $\pi_i$ and put $e_i=v_i(x)>0$. Its residue field is $L_i$, since localization at $Q_i$ inverts exactly the nonzero classes of $E/Q_i$. Let $e$ be a positive common multiple of the $e_i$. For $0\le k\le e$ set $n_i(k)=\lceil ke_i/e\rceil$ and define the $A$-submodule $F_k=\{t\in T:t_\eta\in\pi_i^{n_i(k)}E_{Q_i}\text{ for every }i\}$. Thus $F_0=T$. The primary intersection formula of Step 4 and [lem-per-formal-boundary-power-detection] at $n=1$ give $F_e=xT$. For $k\ge1$, $t\in F_k$ implies $v_i(t_\eta^e)\ge ke_i$ for all $i$ by [lem-sc-dvr-valuation-arithmetic]. Apply [lem-trf-krull-principal-primary-decomposition] to $x^k$ (with the same height-one primes) to obtain $t_\eta^e\in x^kE$. Power detection now gives a unique $u\in T$ with $t^e=x^ku$; uniqueness follows from injectivity of multiplication by $x$. For $k=0$ put $u=t^e$.

source.place: Agent valuation filtration using Proposition 4.10.3 for x and x^k; DVR valuations use Stacks 00PD and 031T, as in the cited principal-divisor node.

proof.text: Fix $0\le k<e$. The integer $n_i(k+1)-n_i(k)$ is $1$ precisely for $i$ in $I_k=\{i:e\mid ke_i\}$, and is $0$ otherwise (because $e_i\mid e$). For $i\in I_k$ set $a_i=ke_i/e$ and define $z_i(t)$ to be the residue of $t_\eta/\pi_i^{a_i}$ in $L_i$, for $t\in F_k$. These are $A$-linear maps, with scalar action through $A\to R_i\subset L_i$. Their joint kernel is exactly $F_{k+1}$, by the definition of $F_k$ and the above ceiling calculation. Consequently they induce an injective $A$-linear map $F_k/F_{k+1}\to\prod_{i\in I_k}L_i$. The empty product here is the zero module, and then $F_k=F_{k+1}$.

source.place: Agent leading-coefficient calculation in the chosen discrete valuation rings; no finiteness of the quotient is assumed.

proof.text: For $i\in I_k$, put $c_{i,k}=\operatorname{res}_{Q_i}(\pi_i^{ke_i}/x^k)\in L_i^\times$, taking $c_{i,0}=1$. The element is nonzero because numerator and denominator have the same valuation. For $t\in F_k$ and $u$ from Step 7, reduction of $u_\eta=t_\eta^e/x^k$ gives $\overline{u_\eta}=c_{i,k}z_i(t)^e$. Step 6 gives $\overline{u_\eta}\in N_i$. As $\operatorname{Frac}(N_i)=L_i$, write $c_{i,k}=a/b$ with nonzero $a,b\in N_i$, and take $d_{i,k}=a$. Then $d_{i,k}^e/c_{i,k}=a^{e-1}b\in N_i$, so $(d_{i,k}z_i(t))^e\in N_i$. The element $d_{i,k}z_i(t)$ is a root of $X^e-(d_{i,k}z_i(t))^e\in N_i[X]$, hence lies in $N_i$ by its integral closedness from Step 5. Thus $z_i(F_k)\subseteq d_{i,k}^{-1}N_i$. This bounds every valuation layer, including the nilpotent layers of $E/xE$, by a fixed finite module.

source.place: Agent explicit power and denominator calculation from Steps 5–7 and the definition of integral closedness; no extraction of roots or separability is used.

proof.text: For each $k$, the finite product $M_k=\prod_{i\in I_k}d_{i,k}^{-1}N_i$ is a finite $A/xA$-module: a finite generating set for each $N_i$ from Step 5, divided by $d_{i,k}$ and placed in its product coordinate, generates it; $x\in P_i$ kills each coordinate. Steps 8–9 embed $F_k/F_{k+1}$ in $M_k$. The ring $A/xA$ is Noetherian, since its ideals correspond to ideals of $A$ containing $xA$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] gives finite generation of every $F_k/F_{k+1}$ over $A/xA$. The short exact sequences $0\to F_{k+1}/F_e\to F_k/F_e\to F_k/F_{k+1}\to0$, descending from $F_e/F_e=0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-extension-of-finite] prove $F_0/F_e=T/xT$ finite over $A/xA$. This deduction uses the residue comparison and all its higher layers explicitly.

source.place: Tags 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic) and 0519 (lemma-extension), applied to the finite filtration just constructed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] with $I=(x)$ and $M=T$. The ring $A$ is $I$-adically complete by hypothesis; Step 3 gives $\bigcap_nI^nT=0$; Step 10 proves $T/IT$ finite over $A/I$. Its three hypotheses hold, hence $T$ is finite over $A$.

source.place: Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring), with all three hypotheses supplied before it is applied.

proof.text: Let $q$ be minimal over $xT$. Step 4 and [lem-per-formal-boundary-power-detection] at $n=1$ give an injective ring map $T/xT\to E/xE$. The quotient correspondence makes $q/xT$ a minimal prime of $T/xT$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-minimal-prime-lift] there is a prime $Q\subset E$ containing $x$ whose inverse image in $T$ is $q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], choose $Q_0\subseteq Q$ minimal over $xE$. Its inverse image in $T$ is a prime containing $xT$ and contained in $q$, hence equals $q$ by minimality. Therefore $q\cap A=Q_0\cap A\in\Delta$.

source.place: Tags 00FK (lemma-injective-minimal-primes-in-image) and 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology (4)); the original accepted minimality argument.
